chunks.title: [Henan University of Engineering x CLO] Only retain one front panel dart at the waist
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Waist Dart Transformation This section explains the process of converting a garment style to have only one front panel dart at the waist, focusing on dart manipulation, pattern adjustment, and 3D modeling techniques. Key terms include waist dart, A-thumb (a dart-related point), yǒu lóng sǎng (袖龙嗓, a dart or seam term), BP point (bust point), and 3D window simulation. --- ## Overview of Dart Adjustment and Pattern Simplification The style discussed retains only one waist dart. Initially, the sleeve dart and armhole dart from the original circle style are removed, indicating their dart volume has been transferred to the waist dart. This simplifies the dart distribution on the garment. - The sleeve dart is eliminated, and its volume is transferred to the waist. - The armhole dart is removed, effectively deleting that dart and reducing complexity. - This change affects the armhole shape and sleeve fit. --- ## 3D Pattern Manipulation Procedure Using 3D pattern software, the original dart circle is created and then edited: 1. **Select and Delete Middle Part** The middle part of the dart circle is deleted to facilitate reshaping. 2. **Repositioning and Merging Lines** Two lines are aligned and merged to form a new dart shape. 3. **Adjusting Points and Edges** Points are deleted or adjusted to ensure the edges match precisely (measured as 8.3 units on both sides). 4. **Rotating Dart Segments** - Select edges using Shift + right mouse button. - Rotate the dart “thumb”—a control point representing dart manipulation—back to the starting point. - The rotation affects only the small dart piece; the front and middle parts remain unchanged. - This rotation aligns the dart at the yǒu lóng sǎng joint. --- ## Positioning the Waist Dart Relative to the Bust Point (BP) - The waist dart is positioned slightly below the BP point, approximately 1 to 2 cm lower, creating a softer shape. - The “thumb” is transferred to the left side, reflecting the dart movement. - The original A-thumb (an auxiliary dart or dart point) remains initially and needs removal later. --- ## Finalizing Dart Transfer and Cleanup - After transferring the dart volume, the original A-thumb is deleted to avoid redundancy. - The inner line related to the original dart is also deleted. - The transferred dart and the original A-thumb combine to form a larger, single waist dart. - The paper pattern is cut accordingly, then opened symmetrically. --- ## Seam Line Adjustment After Dart Transfer - Side seams and gold lines are reseamed to accommodate the new dart structure. - Check for missing seam lines, especially related to the deleted A-thumb. - Pull up the seam line where the A-thumb was originally located to restore proper seam alignment. --- ## 3D Simulation and Final Verification - Open the 3D window and enable arrangement points to simulate the new pattern. - The final shape shows the transformation of multiple darts into a single waist dart.

chunks.content: --- ## Seam Line Adjustment After Dart Transfer - Side seams and gold lines are reseamed to accommodate the new dart structure. - Check for missing seam lines, especially related to the deleted A-thumb. - Pull up the seam line where the A-thumb was originally located to restore proper seam alignment. --- ## 3D Simulation and Final Verification - Open the 3D window and enable arrangement points to simulate the new pattern. - The final shape shows the transformation of multiple darts into a single waist dart. - The circle pattern after transformation is consistent with the original dart volume but simplified for design and construction. --- ## Summary This process demonstrates how to consolidate sleeve and armhole darts into one waist dart using 3D pattern manipulation. Key steps include deleting unnecessary dart parts, rotating and repositioning dart thumb points, removing redundant lines, reseaming, and verifying the pattern in 3D simulation. This method simplifies the garment’s front panel while maintaining fit and shape integrity.
